findings: The T9/0.5.2 retain-all-logs rule was a temporary safety boundary from before exact dedicated-log recovery was available.
The v0.8.0 implementation can identify and recover exact full-UUID thread-linked log rows during permanent deletion without granting logs-only batch deletion.
Memory and non-thread-owned logs remain outside the mutation boundary, and SQLite logical deletion does not prove physical-byte erasure.
fixes: Permanent deletion removes only exact logs.thread_id rows for explicitly selected full session UUIDs.
Trash and restore retain linked logs; final purge deletes them only when no live session or other recoverable trash entry protects the same ID.
Public compatibility guidance now marks the earlier retain-all-logs rule as superseded while preserving it as historical evidence.
postFixVerification: The compatibility validator requires this public decision record and all six lifecycle policy markers.
The public compatibility README and historical future-project plan distinguish exact lifecycle cleanup from logs-only inventory.
Memory remains read-only and the public safety boundary promises logical row deletion only.
